21.0.s.en: (1) Israel's regret at the extinction of Benjamin

21.0.0.en: After the victory of the tribes, the men of the children of Israel swore that none of the tribes would give his daughter as a wife to any man of the tribe of Benjamin.

21.1.0.en: The tribes of Israel gathered before the tent of the Lord at Bethel, and they repented and wept over the loss of so many in this war and because the tribe of Benjamin was nearing extinction, since they had killed most of its men.

21.2.0.en: They spent their night at Bethel, and in the morning they built an altar to the Lord and offered burnt offerings on it in atonement for the sins into which the people had fallen and seeking forgiveness, and they also offered peace offerings in thanks to the Lord for giving them the victory.

21.3.0.en: When the Levite sent pieces of his wife's body to the tribes, their chiefs threatened that anyone who did not gather to fight Benjamin would be put to death as his punishment.

21.3.1.en: The children of Israel were hasty in swearing to kill anyone who did not take part in the war (v. 5), and they were also hasty in swearing not to intermarry with the women of Benjamin (v. 1), and at the same time they repented because Benjamin was nearing extinction. So do not be hasty in issuing decisions, lest they be wrong or conflict with one another and you then return and regret them. Take care to pray and think well before any decision, and even consult in great decisions.

21.4.0.en: There is one tribe lacking in Israel this day: one of their tribes has perished.

21.4.1.en: Despite the victory the tribes achieved over the tribe of Benjamin, they regretted the loss of one of the twelve tribes, and they felt remorse for their excess in punishing, since they killed even those of this tribe who had not gone out to the war.

21.5.0.en: After the killing of all the women of Benjamin and the tribes' oath not to give their daughters to a Benjamite man (v. 1), they repented and were perplexed: how could the marriage of the remaining six hundred men of the tribe be arranged (ch. 20:47), so that the tribe would not perish completely?

21.6.0.en: What one of the tribes: this means a tribe or a family.

21.6.1.en: Jabesh-gilead: one of the cities of the mountains of Gilead, which lie east of the Jordan and belong to the tribe of Gad (Map 11). After the tribes considered how to deal with the problem of Benjamin, they discovered that the people of Jabesh-gilead had not gathered with them at Mizpeh, and therefore the punishment they had sworn, which was to kill them, fell upon them.

21.7.0.en: The tribes remembered that when they were gathered at Mizpeh before the war, they took a count of the tribes, the families, and the inhabitants of the cities of the children of Israel, and found that the inhabitants of the city of Jabesh-gilead had not come. It appears that Jabesh-gilead's not taking part in fighting Benjamin was because of good relations between them, which appeared afterward when King Saul took care to deliver Jabesh-gilead from the hand of the Ammonites (1 Sam 11), and then afterward by Jabesh-gilead's care for the bodies of Saul's sons whom the Philistines had killed (1 Sam 31:11-13).

21.8.0.en: The tribes rushed to punish the offenders, sending 12 thousand of their valiant soldiers to Jabesh-gilead and commanding them to kill every male in it, whether man or child, and every woman who had been married, and to save alive only the virgin girls.

21.9.0.en: The soldiers went to the city and carried out the mission entrusted to them, and found that the virgin girls numbered 400, so they took them and brought them to "Shiloh," west of the river Jordan, where the tabernacle of meeting was.

21.10.0.en: After the tribes achieved a final victory in the third battle over the children of Benjamin, the excitement of the congregation calmed and the sharpness of their anger against them subsided, so they decided to bring the tribe of Benjamin back to life and not to destroy it. Therefore they sent messengers to the six hundred Benjamite men, who were hiding in the caves of the rock of Rimmon, where they had remained hidden four months, to make peace.

21.10.1.en: Seeking peace with those who have wronged us is a Gospel commandment: "Agree with your adversary quickly, while you are in the way with him" (Mt 5:25), as the Scripture also says: "If your brother shall trespass against you, go and tell him his fault" (Mt 18:15). Whatever dispute arises between us and others, we must seek peace, for a slight dispute, if not settled in its time, may grow into a hard situation that is difficult to remedy. And the Scripture commands us: "Let not the sun go down upon your wrath" (Eph 4:26).

21.11.0.en: They saved alive: they did not kill them.

21.11.1.en: The children of Benjamin responded to the congregation's call and came to Shiloh, and the congregation gave them the girls they had taken from Jabesh-gilead to marry. The number of girls was not enough for all the men, so perhaps they gave them to them by lot.

21.12.0.en: The people grieved over what had happened to the tribe of Benjamin and over this strife in which the rest of the tribes had become involved with this tribe.

21.13.0.en: There was a lack of women for Benjamin: because the women of the tribe of Benjamin had all been killed when the cities of Benjamin were burned.

21.13.1.en: The number of virgin girls handed over to the children of Benjamin to take as wives was not sufficient, for they were 400 girls while the men of Benjamin were 600 men, so the elders of the congregation considered how to arrange the matter for the rest.

21.14.0.en: The chiefs of the congregation decided to preserve all the land that had been the portion of the tribe of Benjamin and give it to the remnant of them who had escaped, to be an inheritance for them as it had been for the whole tribe, so that the tribe would grow again and regain its place among the tribes of the children of Israel.

21.15.0.en: One problem remained unsolved: the need of the remaining men of the tribe for wives, who were two hundred men after the girls were distributed to 400 men. The problem lay in the oath the congregation had sworn not to give their daughters as wives to anyone of Benjamin.

21.16.0.en: Lebonah: it lies about 5 km northwest of Shiloh (Map 10). The chiefs of the congregation began to think how to solve this problem, and their thinking led them to the following: it happened at that time that there was a feast of the Lord in Shiloh, which lies north of Bethel and east of the road connecting Jerusalem and Nablus, and south of a city called "Lebonah." This feast was probably one of the three great feasts, and it may have been the Feast of Tabernacles, in which the dancing of the girls was permitted (v. 21).

21.17.0.en: So the chiefs of the congregation told the two hundred men of the children of Benjamin who remained without wives to hide in the vineyards surrounding Shiloh, and when they saw the daughters of Shiloh coming out to dance in celebration of the feast, to come out from their hiding places, and each one to catch a girl for himself and flee with her to the land of Benjamin to marry her.

21.18.0.en: For ye did not give unto them at this time, that ye should be guilty: you did not give them your daughters by your own will; rather they caught them and fled with them on the same day they were seized, so you have no sin. If the families and relatives of the girls come to complain to us of the seizing of their daughters, we will ask them to forgive you your deed in view of the harsh situation that has befallen you, and of what the congregation did in the height of its anger in killing all the females of the tribe, besides what we swore, not to give our daughters as wives to them, and you did not give them your daughters by your will, but they seized them without your will.

21.19.0.en: The children of Benjamin carried out the plan the elders of Israel had drawn up for them, and each of them seized a girl from among those who came out to dance at Shiloh, and they returned with them to their cities, which had been burned, and settled in them and began to build them and populate them anew.

21.20.0.en: Matters calmed after being inflamed by wars, and the problem of the tribe of Benjamin was solved and it was brought back to life, so the tribes decided to disband their gathering and that each of them should return to the lands of his tribe, so that every individual might carry on his life on his own property.

21.21.0.en: These events took place in the age of the judges, before a king arose, and there was no spiritual leader like Moses and Joshua, but judges who led the congregation and some of the tribes for a limited period, and in the remaining periods they were exposed to deviations such as what happened with the Levite's concubine or the story of Micah.

21.21.1.en: There must be a spiritual leader who leads the Church and leads every family, and even leads your life too, namely your father of confession. So submit to your spiritual father and to the priests and to those in charge in every place, even if you differ with them on some opinions, otherwise your life and the life of the Church will become chaos and all will be exposed to disturbing deviations.
